title: Indian Market News Brief — 11 Nov 2026 — Nifty 50
quick_read: Lower oil prices and strong foreign buying worth Rs 53,739 crore in November can support Indian stock markets. Higher than expected US inflation figures may cause worries about interest rate increases abroad. Company news like raw material cost pressures on tyre makers and rule changes for online insurance sellers may affect specific sectors.

stories.headline: FPIs turn net buyers; pour Rs 53,739 crore in D-Street in Nov so far
stories.summary:
Foreign institutional investors became net buyers in Indian stock markets in November.
They bought shares worth Rs 53,739 crore during the month.
This buying came after global market selling linked to artificial intelligence stocks.
Strong earnings growth and good prices for big Indian companies attracted buyers.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: Large foreign buying shows strong interest and can keep share prices rising in the short term.

stories.headline: Oil prices fall as Trump signals pause in military action against Iran
stories.summary:
Brent crude oil prices fell 1.7 percent to $90.99 per barrel.
West Texas Intermediate oil prices also fell 1.8 percent.
The drop came after comments by Donald Trump about stopping military action against Iran.
Lower oil prices reduce worry about big oil supply cuts from the Middle East.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: Cheaper crude oil lowers cost for Indian fuel companies and cuts national import costs.

stories.headline: US consumer prices rise above expectations in October
stories.summary:
US consumer prices rose by 0.4 percent in October after rising 0.6 percent in September.
This price rise was larger than expected by market experts.
Basic inflation without food and energy also remained high.
The data has raised worries that the US central bank may raise interest rates.
stories.impact: May hurt Nifty: Higher US interest rates can pull global money away from emerging markets like India.

stories.headline: Bajaj Finance issues 5.74 crore warrants to promoter for Rs 5,799 crore
stories.summary:
Bajaj Finance gave 5.74 crore warrants to its main owner Bajaj Finserv.
The total value of the deal is Rs 5,799 crore.
The price set for each warrant is Rs 1,010.
Buyers paid 25 percent of the money now, and the rest is due later.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: Extra money from main owners strengthens the balance sheet of a top Indian financial company.

stories.headline: PB Fintech: Retailers buy, FPIs turn wary in Q2; who got right end of deal?
stories.summary:
PB Fintech shares dropped nearly 49 percent from September levels to Rs 953.80.
The fall happened after insurance regulator IRDAI suggested new rules for selling insurance.
Foreign investors cut their share holdings in the second quarter.
Small retail investors bought more shares during the same period.
stories.impact: May hurt Nifty: Lower share prices and strict regulator rules for insurance distributors can hurt sentiment in digital financial stocks.

stories.headline: Higher input costs drag MRF Q2 net profit down 23%
stories.summary:
Tyre maker MRF reported a 22.8 percent fall in net profit for the July to September quarter.
Operating revenue grew by 17.4 percent to Rs 8,660.19 crore.
Expenses went up significantly due to higher costs for raw materials.
The company announced a dividend of Rs 3 per share.
stories.impact: May hurt Nifty: Rising raw material costs hurting tyre maker profits could worry investors in auto component companies.

stories.headline: NMDC in talks with Russia’s Rosatom to explore lithium mining and processing opportunities
stories.summary:
Government mining company NMDC is holding talks with Russian firm Rosatom.
The discussions are about finding and processing lithium together.
Lithium is a critical metal used in making electric vehicle batteries.
India is trying to secure dependable sources of critical minerals.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: Entry into electric vehicle battery minerals could improve future growth chances for state mining firms.

stories.headline: 37,500 करोड़ रुपये की कोयला/लिग्नाइट सतह आधारित गैसीकरण परियोजनाओं को बढ़ावा देने की योजना का दूसरा चरण सम्‍पन्‍न; एनटीपीसी लिमिटेड की ओर से दो आवेदन प्राप्त, तीसरा चरण आज से आरम्‍भ
stories.summary:
The government finished the second phase of a Rs 37,500 crore project for coal and lignite gasification.
Power producer NTPC submitted two applications under this scheme.
The third phase of the government project started today.
The policy aims to promote cleaner coal technology in India.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: Government funding support for green coal projects helps major state power companies like NTPC.
